MID-SOFFIT.mesh: obSnkSoffit — the rail underside slab under the recess step: 129-137 under the rail top (railBandBot 129 PHOTO; the 8 mm thickness is the construction's own class), |z| 835.1-1010.1; on each long side TWO objects x[−1581.1, −41.9] and x[41.9, 1581.1] — an 83.8 mm GAP at the middle pocket; the ±106 x-figure of the first draft was the end triangles' extent, not a span
MID-SOFFIT.mechanism: the entry ball sits at the gap's edge in plan: under the vertical seat (centre x −30, top 117.5 under) the interference is the slab's inboard END EDGE at x ±41.9 clipping the sphere (nearest point the bottom arris (−41.9, −96.8): −12.6); under V16's seat (centre x −45.4, 3.5 mm outboard of the edge, top 122.4 under) the slab IS overhead and the nearest point is the underside straight above (137 − 122.4 = −14.6). The first draft's '19.5 mm inside the slab' and 'about 55 mm below after the lead' were wrong: 55 was the WIRE line's clearance, not the ball top's.

re_derived_entry_vs_the_soffit.law: ring plane 162 + L_v → the wire line at the run start; ball top = wire − 26.53 (vertical seat) or − 21.6 (V16 seat on the ~36° slope) − 26.25
re_derived_entry_vs_the_soffit.plan: the drop at the rim (x ±44 from the axis on the PHOTO OD 88; ±48 on the BUILT ring, outer diameter 96) puts the entry ball's centre 2-6 mm outboard of the slab's end edge (±41.9), i.e. under the slab in plan: the HEIGHT governs
re_derived_entry_vs_the_soffit.constraint_for_their_re_derivation: ball top ≥ 137 under while |x| > 41.9 − r, i.e. L_v ≥ 27.8 (vertical seat) / 22.9 (V16 seat: 137 + 21.6 + 26.25 − 162 = 22.85) at ring 162; the ring's own ±15 band moves this one-for-one

MID-SOFFIT.owner: ballreturn lane — the chute moves (SNK-R25/R27 re-derivation) against a table-body constraint that is MODEL/PHOTO and stays; the constraint is tight, not removed by the lead
